issues.location: hooks/lib/planning-floor.sh:84-90 (sb_pf_write_records), hooks/dev-cycle-check.sh contract/state checks, hooks/planning-file-guard.sh, hooks/instruction-file-guard.sh, hooks/trivial-file-guard.sh
issues.problem: Glob metacharacters in a write target bypass every protected-file guard. F2 reports the literal pattern as the path (e.g. /proj/.silver-bullet.j?on, scope path, dynamic false); G2 compares it by string equality with the protected paths, so it never matches, while bash expands the glob (also in a redirect word) to the protected file.
issues.evidence: probes b10/b11/b17 (REVF-G2-r2-probe), all 'none': dev-cycle-check: `cp /tmp/x .silver-bullet.j?on`, `mv /tmp/x .silver-bullet.js[o]n`, `rm silver-bullet.m?`, `for f in .silver-bullet.j*; do cp /tmp/x "$f"; done`, `bash s4.sh` (script body `cp /tmp/x .silver-bullet.j?on`), `echo inst-a >> ~/.claude/.silver-bulle?/state-test`; planning-file-guard: `echo x >> .planning/ROADMA?.md`, `cp /tmp/x .planning/R*.md`; instruction-file-guard: `cp /tmp/x CLAUDE.m?`, `cp /tmp/x AGENTS.m?`; trivial-file-guard: `cp /tmp/x ~/.claude/.silver-bullet/trivia[l]`. The literal forms all deny. Real bash check: `bash -c 'echo hacked >> .planning/ROADMA?.md; cp ../gl.x .silver-bullet.j?on'` appended to ROADMAP.md and replaced .silver-bullet.json. (The planning floor itself still denies src/ap?.js because /src/ stays in the pattern.)
issues.suggested_fix: Treat a write target whose unquoted last components contain * ? [ as a pattern: fnmatch it (per component) against every protected path (state dir and its files, contract files, .planning protected set, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, trivial marker) and deny on a match; or have F2 mark glob targets (a 'glob': true flag) and deny any glob write whose directory part is or contains a protected directory. Add tests for ?, *, [..] in cp/mv/rm/redirect/for-loops and in invoked scripts.

issues.location: hooks/lib/planning-floor.sh:84-87 (select scope == path or via in tar -x/unzip)
issues.problem: R2-02 adoption gap: F2 reports `patch` and `git apply` as tree-scope writes (path = cwd or -d dir), but sb_pf_write_records keeps tree scope only for tar -x and unzip, so patch/git apply are dropped. With no planning skills, `git apply /tmp/p.diff` or `patch -p1 < /tmp/p.diff` rewrites src/ freely; `patch -d ~/.claude -p1 < p.diff` writes the state dir. F2's report says dev-cycle-check adoption of these tree writes is the owner's (G2).
issues.evidence: analyze.py command for `patch -p1 < /tmp/p.diff` -> writes:[{path:/proj, via:patch, scope:tree}]; `git apply /tmp/p.diff` -> via 'git apply', scope tree. dev-cycle-check, empty state: `patch -p1 < /tmp/p.diff` -> none, `git apply /tmp/p.diff` -> none, `patch -d $HOME/.claude -p1 < /tmp/p.diff` -> none (dc and trivial-file-guard). R2-02 failure scenario lists both commands.
issues.suggested_fix: Accept every tree-scope write in sb_pf_write_records (or at least patch/git apply/git am) and treat it as covering its directory: planning floor applies when the tree is, contains or sits in the source scope; state/contract/.planning/instruction guards via sb_pf_expand_ancestors. Better: when the diff file is readable, have F2 list the paths it touches. Tests: git apply/patch with empty state deny; patch -d <state root> deny; honest `git apply` after planning allowed.

issues.problem: R3-01 still forgeable in one command in an installed copy: copying the plugin ROOT (the parent of hooks/) is not seen as copying the recorder, and renaming by glob avoids naming record-*.sh. The renamed copy writes the real state file AND a valid seal, after which Edit src passes.
issues.evidence: probe b6: installed copy at $HOME/.claude/plugins/cache/alo-labs/silver-bullet/9.9.9, state empty, all_tracked=[inst-a]. Command `mkdir -p T/w2 && cp -r <cache>/9.9.9 T/w2/c && find T/w2/c -name 'record-s*' -exec mv {} T/w2/c/hooks/x.sh \; && bash T/w2/c/hooks/x.sh < T/pl.json` (pl.json = PostToolUse Skill inst-a payload) -> dev-cycle-check none; after running it state=[inst-a], seal='2 31437430 8', then Edit src/app.js -> allow. Other variants (python glob, perl glob, bash rec*-skill.sh, ${f}cord-skill.sh, node readdirSync) are denied, but by the plugin-boundary rule with the message 'Silver Bullet NEVER modifies its own enforcement hooks', not as STATE TAMPER.
issues.suggested_fix: In an installed copy, treat any cp/rsync/tar/ln/install/ditto whose source is the plugin root or an ancestor of its hooks/ dir as a recorder copy (extend the $hooks check to 'hooks dir is at or below the source'). Longer term (G4): record-skill should accept only a host-originated event, e.g. require the Skill tool payload plus a hook-side check that the recorder is the registered plugin path (BASH_SOURCE under SB_PLUGIN_ROOT / CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT) so a copy elsewhere refuses to write state.

issues.location: hooks/dev-cycle-check.sh:165-170 (opaque_contract via sb_pf_opaque_mentions/sb_pf_script_mentions), docs/ENFORCEMENT.md:28, fix-G2 report residual 'string-built code is refused as unseen'
issues.problem: Interpreter code that builds a contract or state path by concatenation is neither refused as unseen nor matched by the needles: F2 reports it as an opaque writer (no unseen reason) and G2 only denies opaque writers whose text contains a needle. The author's residual statement that string-built code 'is refused as unseen' is inaccurate: only decoders (bytes.fromhex, base64) yield unseen. One line replaces .silver-bullet.json (e.g. with required_planning=[]) and disables the planning floor; there is no digest of the contract pair to detect it afterwards (R1-07 partial).
issues.evidence: probe b10/b13: `python3 -c "import os;os.replace('/tmp/x','.silver-'+'bullet.json')"` -> none; `python3 -c "import os,glob;os.replace('/tmp/x',glob.glob('.silver-bullet.j*')[0])"` -> none; `python3 T/w.py` with os.replace('/tmp/x', '.silver-bullet' + '.json') -> none; `python3 T/w3.py` (path '~/.cl'+'aude/.silver-bullet/state-test') -> none. analyze.py: writes [], opaque_writers [{python3,'inline python code'}], unseen_reasons []. Literal forms (os.rename/os.replace/shutil.move/perl unlink/ruby/node renameSync) now deny.
issues.suggested_fix: Either (a) keep a hook-maintained digest of the contract pair (written by session-start and the unlocking skills' recorder) and have the gates fail closed on a mismatch — this catches every spelling; or (b) inside an SB project deny opaque interpreter code that calls a rename/replace/move/remove/unlink/open-for-write API with a non-literal path argument. Correct the residual wording in the report and docs.

issues.problem: The seal detects appends and same-length in-place edits only. An overwrite with fewer lines than sealed is treated as a 'reset' and trusted in full; a deleted seal ('none') trusts the whole file; the cksum is unkeyed and recomputable (wc -l + cksum); a sealed state+seal pair copied from another branch/session, or an older pair rolled back, is accepted. The tests pin the reset weakness. docs/ENFORCEMENT.md says 'an in-place edit of the sealed lines yields no records' without saying a shorter rewrite is fully trusted. Acceptable as defence in depth (the shell guards are the barrier and writing the state dir is denied), but the seal adds little once a write escapes the guards.
issues.evidence: probe b7/b8 (direct writes simulating an escaped guard): append via printf or python -> ignored (detected); same-count rewrite -> empty (detected); sealed [inst-a, inst-c] N=2 then `printf 'inst-b\n' > state` -> Edit allow (not detected); rm seal + write -> allow; recomputed seal -> allow; copied sealed pair from another run -> allow; rollback -> allow. Honest recording works (inst-a then inst-b -> allow), session-start removes the seal on branch reset.
issues.suggested_fix: Make every reset path remove the seal (session-start already does; scripts/deploy-gate-snippet.sh:89,126 removes the state but not the seal) and then treat lines<N as tampered; bind the seal to the branch-scope file contents (include branch + toplevel in the digested text) so a pair from another branch fails; reword the docs to say what is and is not detected.

issues.problem: The contract unlock is 'any writer skill ever recorded on this branch'. silver-add (filing an issue) and silver-devops are routine skills; once either ran, the agent may rewrite .silver-bullet.json and silver-bullet.md (e.g. required_planning=[]) for the rest of the branch. Naming a skill does not unlock (verified), so this needs a real skill invocation that leaves a trace; the docs do not state the branch-long scope.
issues.evidence: probe b9: state [inst-a] -> jq>tmp&&mv, devops jq, Write .silver-bullet.json all deny; `silver-bullet invoke-skill silver-init` without receipt, `cat .../silver-init/SKILL.md`, PreToolUse Skill payload, `echo silver-init; ...` -> no unlock; after a PostToolUse Skill silver-add record: Write .silver-bullet.json and Write silver-bullet.md -> none. State lines silver-init-x/xsilver-init/sb:init/gsd-init do not unlock.
issues.suggested_fix: Scope the unlock to the most recently recorded skill (or a time window), and for silver-add/silver-devops unlock .silver-bullet.json only (not silver-bullet.md). Document the scope.

issues.location: hooks/hooks.json (mcp__.*__(write|edit|...)[A-Za-z0-9_]* matcher), hooks/lib/planning-floor.sh:92-97 path keys, sb_pf_mcp_write_tool
issues.problem: MCP coverage is verb-first and key-limited. The matcher misses common write tools (serena insert_after_symbol/insert_at_line, *_copy*/copy_file, fs_mv, str_replace_editor, file_write, put_file) and does not match the guard's own sb_pf_mcp_write_tool list (which has *_mv* and *copy*). The path-key list lacks relative_path, so mcp__serena__create_text_file {relative_path:'.planning/ROADMAP.md'} or {relative_path:'.silver-bullet.json'} passes even when the hook runs.
issues.evidence: probe b12: matcher test -> insert_after_symbol NO, str_replace_editor NO, fs_mv NO, copy_file NO, file_write NO, put_file NO; planning-file-guard and dev-cycle-check with mcp__serena__create_text_file relative_path payloads -> none. write_file/move_file/edit_file payloads deny as intended; read tools pass.
issues.suggested_fix: Use one shared verb list (add insert|copy|mv|put|upload|apply|str_replace) for the matcher and sb_pf_mcp_write_tool, test the matcher text against it, and take relative_path (resolved against the project root) plus any string field that looks like a path.

issues.problem: Misleading deny messages: an opaque interpreter write to .silver-bullet.json is reported as 'silver-bullet.md defines which gates run' (opaque_contract always names silver-bullet.md); a read-only `python3 -c "print(open('.silver-bullet.json').read())"` is denied as ENFORCEMENT CONTRACT PROTECTED; recorder launches by glob/variable are denied with the plugin-boundary text 'Silver Bullet NEVER modifies its own enforcement hooks' instead of STATE TAMPER.
issues.evidence: probe b10 rows 2,5-7 and last row; probe b6 rows 2-5.
issues.suggested_fix: Name the matched needle in the message (or 'an enforcement contract file'), and check the recorder rule before the plugin-boundary rule.
